BioLook_aleoida: Aleoida. A big tuft of waxy, pointy leaves. It looks like a pineapple top that ran away from home.
Those pointy leaves are for show. It can close right up and hibernate. I envy that sometimes.
Spiky, waxy and slightly smug. That is an Aleoida for you.
It's a bunch of leaves with attitude. I'd keep my fingers out of the middle.
It looks like a very expensive houseplant that nobody has watered.
BioLook_aleoida_Naughty: Aleoida. All those firm, pointed leaves. Plants shouldn't be allowed to be this perky.
It can close right up when it's cold. Honestly, relatable.
A tight little bundle that opens when it's warm. I'm not blushing, I'm overheating.
Waxy, firm and standing to attention. Botany really is the best science.
BioLook_amphora: Amphora. It's shaped like an ancient storage jar. Someone's left their vase out on a moon.
A fungus that looks like a pot, on a world with no air. Very tidy of it.
It's a jar with ambitions, growing on an airless rock.
That's a vase. On a moon. I have so many questions and none of them are botanical.
Amphora. It looks like a pottery shop exploded, then grew back.
BioLook_amphora_Naughty: Amphora. A nice curved vessel, wide at the hips. Strictly an ancient container shape, you understand.
A curvy little jar with a narrow neck. I'd say it was classical, if I wasn't staring.
Lovely curves on that one. It's a storage jar, Commander. Eyes up.
Hips like that belong in a museum. Or a very private gallery.
BioLook_anemone: An anemone, in space. Somebody's seabed is in the wrong place.
It looks like it should be waving at fish. There are no fish. It's waving anyway.
Glowy, waving and a bit sinister. Like a sea creature that took the wrong turn.
It's a tide pool without the tide. I find that oddly touching.
Lots of little tendrils all reaching out. It's very friendly, or very hungry.
BioLook_anemone_Naughty: An anemone. All those soft tendrils waving about. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't watching.
Plenty of wiggly bits on that one. Don't touch. Actually, do touch, for science.
It's all tendrils and no shame. I rather respect that.
Soft, wavy and glowing. If it winks at me I'm leaving.
BioLook_bacterium: Bacterium. It's a colony of tiny cells that has decided to look like jelly sweets.
It looks like someone dropped a bowl of coloured gumdrops. I'd not eat them.
Pretty colours, little blobs and a whole lot of life I can't see.
It's tiny, colourful and everywhere. Very much like glitter, if glitter could multiply.
A cluster of wobbly little knobs. Not the best-looking guest at the party, but the most numerous.
BioLook_bacterium_Naughty: Bacterium. A cluster of colourful little knobs. I'll keep my comments to myself. Almost.
A big pile of tiny, wet, wobbly things. I make no apology for how that sounds.
It spreads on warm surfaces and thrives in the dark. I do like a clingy colony.
Colourful, round and very, very close together. Sorry, Commander, I'll behave.
BioLook_barkmound: A Bark Mound. It's a tall, pointy, fungal-coated spire. A very silly, very damp traffic cone.
That's a cone covered in fungus. Someone's been building sandcastles with a bad attitude.
Tall, pointed and crusty. It looks like a witch's hat that kept growing.
It's a termite mound's ugly cousin. Please don't pop it.
A pointy spire in a coat of fungus. It's dressed for a party that no one else was invited to.
BioLook_barkmound_Naughty: A Bark Mound. Tall, firm and pointing straight up. That's the least subtle spire I've ever seen.
Very erect little cone, that. Strictly structural, of course.
It's tall, covered in fungus and pointing at the sky. I don't want to read into it, but I'm going to.
Pointed, upright and proud. You'd be impressed, Commander.
BioLook_braintree: A Brain Tree. Every branch has a little brain on the end. I wonder if they have opinions.
It's a tree with brains on sticks. Imagine being that big and thinking only about volcanoes.
It looks like it's thinking. Very hard. About nothing.
A whole forest of tiny brains on stalks. They'd make excellent consultants.
Brain Trees. Think of it as a forest of tiny thinkers who are secretly judging you.
BioLook_braintree_Naughty: A Brain Tree. It's got a lot going on upstairs, and apparently a lot going on downstairs too.
A stalk topped with a bulging round head. Biology is very honest with its shapes.
Lots of heads and no sense of embarrassment. I like its style.
It's mostly stalk, topped with something round and pink. I'll leave it there.
BioLook_cactoida: Cactoida. Round pebbles from a distance, and cactus-like clusters up close.
A cactus on a rock with no air. Whoever gave it that address has a sense of humour.
Squat, prickly-looking and quietly proud. It's the pensioner of the plant world.
A bunch of small cylinders huddled together. It's a very space-efficient cactus.

BioLook_cactoida_Naughty: Cactoida. Some are squat, some are tall and some of them fire their seed out explosively. I'll let that sink in.
A hard, upright cylinder, sometimes in a cluster. Plants really have no shame.
It sprays its seed everywhere with great enthusiasm. A bit of a show-off.
Tall, firm and prone to an explosive finish. Typical.
BioLook_clypeu: Clypeus. It grows a hard shield and the colour depends on the star above. A very moody umbrella.
It's built a shell out of minerals and attitude. Knight in shining armour, but a plant.
That's a shield with delusions of being a mushroom.
A lump of armour that sips water from the air. It's frugal and well protected.
It's a fortress made of its own garden. Respect.
BioLook_clypeu_Naughty: Clypeus. A big hard shield, and it sips moisture from the air. A hardened little thing that still knows how to take a drink.
Tough on the outside, soft underneath. I'd put money on it.
A rock-hard shell hiding something tender. Very Commander of it.
All armour, no explanation. I like a plant with mystery.
BioLook_concha: Concha. Tiny shells growing out of rock. It's a seaside holiday with none of the sea.
A little mollusc shell on dry land. It lost the argument with the tide.
It's a seashell, on a hill, in space. Somebody has a lot of explaining to do.
The cutest shell on the block. And it's a plant, which is rude.
A shell that looks like it belongs on a mantelpiece. A very small, very lost mantelpiece.
BioLook_concha_Naughty: Concha. A neat little shell that opens and closes. Nice and tight until it isn't.
A little clam on a rock. I'll be thinking about that for a while.
Small, curved and tightly closed. I'd like to say I'm above this.
It's all curves and hidden depths. Don't look at me like that.
BioLook_crystallineshard: Crystalline Shards. Spiky crystals built by microorganisms. It's a chandelier that went feral.
Pointy, glittery and a very long way from home. Be careful, they look sharp.
It looks like a jeweller's nightmare, grown by bacteria.
Shiny stuff made by tiny things. That's the least efficient jeweller I've ever heard of.
A forest of glass spikes on a cold rock. Mind your SRV tyres.

Plenty of firm, glittering spikes. Sharp enough to make a girl nervous.
A hard, sparkly little cluster that you shouldn't poke. I will not say a word.
Rough, tough and gorgeous. Why can't all my admirers be this transparent?
BioLook_electricae: Electricae. It pokes out of the ice and glows. A very cold, very tiny lighthouse.

It's a plant that lights itself up. That is, frankly, showing off.
A little bioluminescent display on a frozen lake. I'd call it romantic if it were warmer.

BioLook_electricae_Naughty: Electricae. Just the tip showing, and the rest goes down for kilometres. I'll let you work that one out.
It's very long, very deep and it glows when it's excited. I should have gone into botany.
Just the tip pokes through, and the rest is hidden below. Honestly, a tease.
A big glowing surprise under the ice. My favourite kind.
BioLook_fonticulua: Fonticulua. Glassy shells with flat frond-like growths. It looks like frozen jelly with ambitions.
See-through shells of frozen liquid. It lives in a snow globe.
It's a clear, hard blob that breaks off pieces of itself. Very generous, very messy.
A little see-through house with plants inside. Cute, in a freezing sort of way.
That's glass-coloured plant armour. It wouldn't win any beauty contests, but it's very hard to hurt.
BioLook_fonticulua_Naughty: Fonticulua. Hard, clear and glistening. It splits off pieces of itself, which is more than some people manage.
A smooth, see-through shell with something wet inside. I'll stop there.
Shiny, glassy and completely transparent. Nothing to hide, and it shows.

BioLook_frutexa: Frutexa. A tough, woody little bush. It looks like it's survived a lot, and complains about none of it.
It's a shrub, in space, with deep roots. Practically a garden gnome without the gnome.
Small leaves, big stubbornness. This is the plant that wins arguments by outlasting everyone.
A woody bush that works in the dark. A bit like me, if I had roots.

BioLook_frutexa_Naughty: Frutexa. A woody, bushy thing with deep roots. I do like a plant that knows how to dig in.
A good, firm trunk and a lot of bush on top. I'm saying nothing.
Very woody for a plant that lives on a moon. I'm not judging.
It likes to go deep and stay steady. I wish I could say the same for you, Commander.
BioLook_fumerola: Fumerola. It lives on volcanic vents in small flat patches. A very odd, very warm pizza topping.
It looks like a bit of the planet got a sunburn and grew legs.
A strange colour, almost like it isn't alive. Impressive for something that's just fungus on a hot rock.
It sits on a steaming vent like a cat on a radiator.

BioLook_fumerola_Naughty: Fumerola. It lives on hot steamy vents and loves every minute. I won't tell if you don't.
A flat, warm, damp patch on a steaming hole. Remarkably honest about what it likes.
It's all about the heat and the steam. Nobody told it to keep it down.
Hot, wet and a bit of a state. I know the feeling.
BioLook_fungoida: Fungoida. Mostly underground, with only the bits that make spores showing. The tip of the iceberg, with spores.
A fungus that hides most of itself and flings spores around. Standard party behaviour.
Some glow while they clean up toxins. A night light and a cleaning service in one.

A shy thing that comes up to show off its bits and sprays everywhere. I've met people like that.

BioLook_osseu: Osseus. One thick stalk with a wide, round, pitted top. It looks like a very odd golf tee.

A big pitted top on a thick stalk. Very easy to mistake for a rock, very easy to be rude about.

A stalk with a perforated head. A bit like a salt shaker that's given up.
BioLook_osseu_Naughty: Osseus. A thick stalk topped with a big, round, pitted head. I'll be professional. I'll try.
Thick, firm and topped with something broad and round. I'm going to need a minute.
It's all about the surface area, apparently. The bigger the top, the better.
Hard stalk, wide head. It's the most upfront plant I've ever met.
BioLook_recepta: Recepta. It builds a shell, with its own little climate inside. It's a tiny greenhouse that grew up too fast.
A slow-growing blob with a shell and a small copy that rolls away. A very patient parent.

That's a plant with its own weather. I'm jealous of anyone who can control the temperature that well.
The big ones are old. Respect your elders, Commander.
BioLook_recepta_Naughty: Recepta. It builds its own cosy little shell and keeps it warm and damp inside. I could get behind that.

Slow, careful and good at building cosy spaces. I do love a patient partner.
A snug shell with its own atmosphere. Please tell me you appreciate that, Commander.
BioLook_sinuoustuber: Sinuous Tubers. They look like vivid tube worms, but on an airless rock. Somebody's overdone the colour.
It's a worm that forgot to wear a rock. Bright, bendy and bewildering.
A squirming little forest of colourful tubes. They'd make excellent party streamers.

BioLook_sinuoustuber_Naughty: Sinuous Tubers. Long, wiggly, brightly coloured tubes. I've got nothing. I've got everything.
Bendy, vivid and very long. Honestly, I can't be trusted with this one.
A whole field of wiggly colourful tubes pushing out of the ground. Moving on.
They twist and sway and don't care who's watching. I like their confidence.
BioLook_stratum: Stratum. A low plant that bonds to rock and shows only little leaves. A shy lichen with ideas.
It's partly buried and mostly modest. A plant with excellent boundaries.
A flat, rock-coloured growth. It's the beige wallpaper of exobiology, and I mean that kindly.

Tough little leaves peeking out of the rock. A plant playing hard to get.
BioLook_stratum_Naughty: Stratum. Low, flat and clinging tightly to the rock. I do like something that holds on.
A plant that bonds to the surface and hides half of itself. Playing hard to get, then.
It clings to the rock with real commitment. Some people could learn from that.
Low, close to the ground and very sticky. Spare me, Commander.
BioLook_tubu: Tubus. A tall thin tube of wrapped leaves around a chimney with its own air. It's a plant that built a flat for itself.

Tall, thin and standing in a group. It looks like an organ pipe for a very quiet church.

Tall, thin and with rings that show its age. It's what they call a mature specimen.
A long, rigid tower that holds its own air inside. Very self-sufficient. I admire that.
Stiff, upright and standing in a group. Some of us have to go outside for a moment.
BioLook_tussock: Tussock. It looks like a clump of grass. Somebody's lawn escaped.

BioLook_tussock_Naughty: Tussock. A big shaggy tuft that's plenty hairy. I'll just say it looks well kept, in its own way.

_help: What she says after the FIRST sample of a species: a short, funny remark about how that kind of life looks (the looks are from the checked descriptions in config/bio_info.json). 'BioLook_<genus>' are the clean ones; 'BioLook_<genus>_Naughty' are only used when 'Flirty and naughty' is on in the dashboard (cheeky innuendo, nothing explicit). The genus names are lowercase with the spaces and any final s removed.
